# Components

Which components the system carries: its inventory, picked from the catalogue.

## The five answers

| Question | Answer | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which component families does it need? | Core, plus content and media | Product teams build sign-up and account forms, plus product pages with questions and faces. |
| How far does the inventory reach? | What today's screens use, plus what the next ones will likely need | Three product teams find their next parts ready, kept by one platform team. |
| How does a component earn its place? | Its family is in the roles, so product teams find it ready | Product teams find a whole family ready instead of asking one by one. |
| When does a component get another look? | Also for emphasis and size | Variants for emphasis and size let each brand feel present without new components. |
| Where do components do the most work? | Sign-up and account pages | Most components sit in sign-up and account pages. |

| `size.16` | 1rem (16px) | <span class="ods-bar" style="width:1rem"></span> |
| `size.44` | 2.75rem (44px) | <span class="ods-bar" style="width:2.75rem"></span> |
| `size.48` | 3rem (48px) | <span class="ods-bar" style="width:3rem"></span> |
| `space.16` | 1rem (16px) | <span class="ods-bar" style="width:1rem"></span> |
| `space.24` | 1.5rem (24px) | <span class="ods-bar" style="width:1.5rem"></span> |
| `space.8` | 0.5rem (8px) | <span class="ods-bar" style="width:0.5rem"></span> |

</div>

## Where it lands

- Button
- Input
- Control
- Badge
- Card
- Table
- Tabs
- Overlay

## When to use what

| Situation | Use | Not | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| No component in the inventory fits | a component from the inventory with brand tokens | a component made for one brand | Brands change primitives, never components; one brand-only part breaks the shared library. |
